## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to design a practical multilingual NLP solution under real-time constraints with privacy considerations—skills essential for consumer-facing products at major tech companies.

## Key Concepts
- **Multilingual NLP:** Language detection, TF-IDF vectorization, and logistic regression enable efficient intent classification across languages.
- **Latency Constraints:** Lightweight models (TF-IDF + LR) achieve sub-200ms CPU inference, making them suitable for real-time chat applications.
- **Data Labeling:** Use human-in-the-loop labeling or pre-trained multilingual models to generate initial labels, then refine with active learning.
- **Privacy Constraints:** Anonymize PII before processing, comply with GDPR/CCPA by storing minimal data, and consider on-device inference for sensitive use cases.
- **Evaluation:** Track macro-F1 across both languages to ensure balanced performance regardless of class distribution or language-specific nuances.

# Why This Is Asked
Tests on-device NLP design under tight resources, multilinguality, and privacy. Candidates must justify model choices, quantization, drift detection, and OTA rollout.

# Key Concepts
- On-device inference with resource constraints
- Multilingual encoders and lightweight NLU
- Model compression: distillation, quantization, pruning
- Drift detection and secure OTA updates
- Privacy-preserving embeddings and offline-first architecture

# Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo on-device inference outline
function infer(uttTokens, model) {
  const emb = model.encode(uttTokens); // quantized
  const intent = model.classify(emb);
  const actions = model.extract(emb);
  return { intent, actions };
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design lightweight, privacy-conscious NLP with practical constraints. 

## Key Concepts
- Text normalization: emoji/slang handling
- Lightweight bilingual features; on-device constraints
- Hybrid rule+ML approach; latency and privacy trade-offs

## Code Example
```python
import re
EMOJI_MAP = {":)": "smile"}
def normalize(text):
  for k,v in EMOJI_MAP.items():
    text = text.replace(k, v)
  text = re.sub(r"[^\w\s]", "", text)
  return text.lower()
```

- Multilingual encoder with shared embeddings

```python
class Pipeline:
    def __init__(self, encoder, ner_head, intent_head):
        ...

        norm = normalize(text)
        emb = encoder.encode(norm, lang)
        ents = ner_head.decode(emb)
        intents = intent_head.predict(emb)
        return ents, intents
```

- **Safe rollback mechanisms**: Implementing safeguards to revert to previous model versions when performance degrades
